q: Which departments is the model losing to the naive baseline, and why might that be?
answer:
Losing on forecast value added (model FA below seasonal-naive FA): HOUSEHOLD_1 (fva -9.4), FOODS_2 (fva -0.9), FOODS_1 (fva -7.3), HOUSEHOLD_2 (fva -7.6) and FOODS_3 (fva -7.0). Only 2 of 7 departments improved (HOBBIES_1 fva 2.8, HOBBIES_2 fva 10.6), and pooled fva is -5.7. Note the losers include the three largest-volume departments (FOODS_3 615655 units, HOUSEHOLD_1 163737, FOODS_2 113746).

Why (hypothesis supported by the daily series, not a measured cause): the model prediction is a single constant within each fold — e.g. FOODS_3 is 2022.6 for all of fold 1, 2497.5 for fold 2, 2431.5 for fold 3 — while actuals in those departments swing widely day to day (FOODS_3 ranges from 1485 to 3221 inside fold 1 alone). A flat forecast carries no day-of-week or holiday signal, whereas the seasonal-naive baseline reproduces last week's weekday shape, so it wins wherever the weekly cycle is strong (FOODS and HOUSEHOLD). The flat forecast is also badly exposed on the closure day: on 2013-12-25 actual is 0 against a model of 2431.5 for FOODS_3 and 646.9 for HOUSEHOLD_1, giving errors of 2431.5 and 646.9. The two departments the model does win are the noisiest/smallest-shape ones (HOBBIES_2 naiveFa is only 54.9), where copying last week is itself unreliable.
